subject: Follow-up: embeddings fit & semantic search benchmarks
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Mallory Chen <mallory@atlasretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 1 May 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: embeddings fit & semantic search benchmarks

Hi Mallory —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can validate model fit for Atlas Retail's product search: 

Summary from call:
- Goal: Improve product-level semantic search relevance (category-agnostic recommendations + typos) and reduce cold-start retrieval errors across SKUs.
- Current infra: Elasticsearch + BM25 + sparse vectors for titles. Average query latency target: < 120ms median; recall@10 target +15% vs current.
- Data: ~1.2M SKUs, product titles + short descriptions (~30-120 tokens), and pairwise click logs for ~6 months.

Recommended evaluation plan (short):
1) Small embedding pilot (10k sample) comparing two Redwood embeddings: rw-embed-small-v1 (512d) and rw-embed-large-v2 (1536d).
2) Metrics: recall@1/5/10, MRR, nDCG@10, cosine similarity distributions, and latency for index lookup (HNSW).
3) Checks: embedding drift (month-over-month), dimensionality trade-offs, and quantization impact (int8 / PQ).
4) Deliverables: benchmark spreadsheet, sample prompt set for contextualizing product metadata, notebook with reproducible evals, and a recommended production config (index type, sharding, shard size).

Attachments I'll send: sample_prompt_set.csv, atlas_semantic_benchmarks_v1.xlsx, and a prototype notebook. I'll also include suggested prompt patterns (title-only vs title+desc vs title+click-context).

Proposed next steps:
- I'll upload the 10k sample results by EOD Monday (May 4).
- Could you confirm the sample slice preferences (random vs heavy-hitter SKUs vs long-tail)?
- If possible, share a sample of click logs schema (anonymized) so we can build evaluation queries that reflect real user intent.

Thanks — feel free to correct anything I missed.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0182

From: Mallory Chen <mallory@atlasretail.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 2 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: embeddings fit & semantic search benchmarks

Thanks Marcus — really helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Sample slice: let's do 70% random, 20% heavy-hitters (top-selling SKUs), 10% cold-long-tail (<=5 views/month).
2) Click logs: we can share an anonymized CSV with columns (query, clicked_sku, timestamp, session_id) — will scrub PII and send by Monday.
3) Latency: 120ms median is a hard target for the web UI; mobile can be a bit higher.

Two asks: 
- Can you include baseline numbers for our current sparse-vector + BM25 approach in the same spreadsheet? We want to see delta columns.
- If you recommend rw-embed-large-v2, we are sensitive to cost & vector storage; please include expected storage and compute estimates for both models.

I'm looping Tom (dataops) to confirm export details.

Thanks — Mallory
Mallory Chen
Head of Search & Personalization | Atlas Retail
mallory@atlasretail.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Mallory Chen <mallory@atlasretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom@dataops.com>
Date: Sat, 2 May 2026 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: embeddings fit & semantic search benchmarks

Mallory —

Great notes. I attached the initial benchmark template and prompt set. High level answers inline: 

- Baseline numbers: included a placeholder sheet with synthetic BM25 + sparse-vector baselines (we'll replace with your exported sample metrics once you send logs).
- Storage/compute estimates: rw-embed-small-v1 (512d) -> ~2 KB per vector (float16 baseline), rw-embed-large-v2 (1536d) -> ~6 KB per vector. With 1.2M SKUs that's ~2.4GB vs ~7.2GB uncompressed; we'll include quantized estimates (int8/PQ) that reduce on-disk size ~4-8x depending on config. Also include estimated QPS cost for batch vs streaming embeddings and CPU/GPU inference notes.

Notes on evaluation choices: 
- HNSW index should be fine for production; we recommend recall tuning via efSearch/efConstruction. For heavy-hitter slices, tune efSearch lower to favor latency; for long-tail, increase efSearch to prioritize recall.
- Dimensionality trade-offs: 512d tends to be faster and cheaper but may lose fine-grained semantic nuance in complex descriptions. 1536d shows higher MRR/nDCG in our retail benchmarks but costs more.
- Drift monitoring: we'll compute centroid shifts and cluster-coverage changes month-over-month and surface regressions (e.g., >5% drop in recall@10 for top-100 queries).

I've uploaded: 
- atlas_semantic_benchmarks_v1.xlsx (sheets: plan, synthetic_baseline, metric_defs)
- sample_prompt_set.csv (title-only, title+desc, title+session-context columns)
- rw-embed-eval-notebook.ipynb (Colab link + instructions in first cell)

Drive links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C_rw-embed-benchmarks (see 'deliverables' folder). HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/HS-2026-0421

Next steps:
- Mallory/Tom: send anonymized click CSV by Monday EOD (May 4).
- We'll run the 10k pilot and post results to the benchmark sheet by EOD Tuesday (May 5).
- Follow-up call to review results and recommended production config — propose Wed May 6 10:00 AM PT.

If that works I'll send a calendar invite.

Best,
Marcus

[Attachment stubs: atlas_semantic_benchmarks_v1.xlsx (xlsx), sample_prompt_set.csv (csv), rw-embed-eval-notebook.ipynb (ipynb)]
